Oronde Gadsden II has room to work — SEA allow 42 yds/game to TE1s (vs ~35), a receiving-yards and target angle.

The SEA host the LAC as favorites of 3.0, with the total set at 45.5 — a market that implies a SEA 24–21 scoreline. Running the game forward from that baseline, we expect a contest that spends roughly 31% of its snaps with SEA in front, 41% within one score, and 27% with SEA chasing. That distribution is the engine of everything below: game state is what turns a team's tendencies into a specific player's workload, so before we get to individuals it's worth being explicit about how this game is likely to be played.

This is a coin-flip script. With only 3.0 points separating them, neither team projects to spend much time in a blowout state — most of the game lives in the 'close' bucket, where play-calling stays balanced and usage tracks each player's established role rather than being distorted by score. In tight games the stars on both sides see their normal, dependable workloads, and there is less garbage-time leakage to backups.

The Key Matchups

Tough sledding for Omarion Hampton — SEA are stingy against the run (106 yds/game, well below the ~120 norm); lean under on his rushing line.

Ladd McConkey faces a tough cover — SEA hold WR1s to just 48 yds/game (vs ~58); a rec-yards under lean.

Game Script, Pace & Environment

A middling 46 total — no strong lean either way; the value is in the individual matchups above, not the game environment.

SEA — a balanced offense

SEA are a balanced offense — their run/pass split by game state tracks the league closely (43% pass when leading vs 44% average), so their players' usage is driven more by role than by any strong situational lean.

Jadarian Price (12 carries, 52 yards) projects to his baseline workload — no strong script push either way in a close game.

Jaxon Smith-Njigba projects for 9 targets and 79 yards, in line with his established role in a script that neither inflates nor suppresses the pass.

Underneath, AJ Barner (TE, 3 targets, 25 yards) is the dependable secondary read — and note the red zone stays TE-friendly regardless of score, so his touchdown equity holds up even if the game script shifts.

LAC — a run-heavy offense

LAC are one of the league's more run-committed offenses: on early downs while leading, they pass just 40% of the time, against a league average of 44% — a genuine clock-bleeding identity, not noise (it holds after shrinking their sample toward the league).

Omarion Hampton (10 carries, 43 yards) projects to his baseline workload — no strong script push either way in a close game.

Ladd McConkey projects for 5 targets and 45 yards, in line with his established role in a script that neither inflates nor suppresses the pass.

Underneath, Oronde Gadsden II (TE, 3 targets, 30 yards) is the dependable secondary read — and note the red zone stays TE-friendly regardless of score, so his touchdown equity holds up even if the game script shifts.

What to watch

The single biggest swing factor is availability — use the injury tool in the sidebar to mark anyone out; a starter's absence doesn't just remove his line, it redistributes his targets and carries to specific teammates, and the report and projections rebuild around it. Beyond that: if this game breaks toward the projected 3-point margin, the garbage-time backups (the ◆-flagged rows below) are where soft lines and real edge tend to appear — those depth players get fed in blowouts, and the market is slowest to price them.

This preview and the projections below regenerate through the week as injuries, weather and line moves update the inputs.
